name: What information should I have ready before meeting a contractor about a home addition or major remodel?

mainEntity.name: What information should I have ready before meeting a contractor about a home addition or major remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Bring a clear list of your goals, rough budget, and any deal-breakers, along with basic property information like address, lot size if you have it, and any known issues. Photos or inspiration images help communicate your style and priorities quickly.

Contractors can give you much better guidance when they understand constraints and expectations up front. You don’t need final answers, but some structure makes the meeting more productive.

Key factors:
- Number of rooms or functions you want to add or change
- Your target budget range and flexibility
- Timing needs (e.g., before a new baby, before selling, or around work schedule)
- Any HOA rules, prior plans, or surveys you may have

Before the meeting, write down your top three goals and any concerns from past projects. Sharing this early allows the contractor to flag feasibility issues and suggest alternatives that better match your budget and timeline.
acceptedAnswer.description: Have your goals, rough budget, timing needs, and any property or HOA details ready before meeting a contractor. A short wish list and a few inspiration photos help them give realistic feedback on costs, feasibility, and options in that first conversation.
